Subject: Hosted API commit question for bursty inference

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. Before we move to procurement, our engineering team asked a few practical questions about annual commits for the hosted API:

- We are a fairly spiky user: predictable base load (Starter/Growth scale) but with frequent bursts during nightly batch scoring and monthly reports. Can you describe how an annual commit handles burst windows? Is there an explicit burst pool or carryover model?
- What are your overage rates and how do they change by tier (Starter/Growth/Enterprise)?
- We need a 12-month ramp with the ability to shift unused tokens into a burst bucket instead of losing them. Any precedent for carryover-to-burst?
- Procurement will ask about SLA credits tied to latency and availability. Do your commit SLAs differ from on-demand?

I attached a rough usage profile to help — can you and your pricing lead suggest a couple of concrete structures (numbers + per-token price) we can show our CFO?

Appreciate it,
Sarah

Hi Sarah — thanks for the profile (very helpful). High level answers first, then a short set of concrete options attached.

Summary: Redwood supports three committed slabs (Starter / Growth / Enterprise). For bursty workloads we offer two complementary mechanisms:

1) Carryover + burst pool: up to 20% of unused monthly committed tokens can be rolled into a dedicated burst pool each month (cumulative up to 3 months), which only applies to token-rate chargebacks and does not change SLAs.
2) Dedicated burst buffer: customers on Growth+ can purchase a small refundable burst credit balance (prepaid) that throttles into the committed lanes automatically when private capacity is saturated.

Proposed sample structures (see attached PDF for math):
- Starter: 250M tokens/year — base $0.0024/token, overage $0.0036/token, no burst buffer included.
- Growth: 1.2B tokens/year — base $0.0018/token, overage $0.0027/token, includes 10% burst pool and 30% ramp carryover for first 6 months.
- Enterprise: custom (>5B) — base $0.0012/token, overage $0.0018/token, includes 20% burst pool, optional dedicated reserved burst buffer, SLA uplift and quarterly usage reviews.

Notes on SLAs: commit customers get a 99.9% uptime SLA for hosted endpoints with credited service-days for significant outages. Latency SLOs are published per-model and we can add a latency SLA for Enterprise with financial credits on miss.

Next steps: I can 1) share a one-page term sheet for each slab, 2) add a refundable burst credit line for Growth, and 3) draft DocuSign-ready terms for procurement. I attached a one-page offer.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments: 20270318-commit-offer-summary.pdf
